title: Point-In-Time Recovery (PITR) Disaster Recovery Architecture
realWorldScenario: At 14:32:10 UTC, a junior developer running an ad-hoc cleanup script accidentally executed `DELETE FROM repayments;` without a WHERE clause in production. Nightly pg_dump backups were taken at 00:00 UTC (14 hours ago).
questionStatement: Design a Point-In-Time Recovery (PITR) procedure to restore the database to 14:32:05 UTC (5 seconds prior to the incident), recovering all 14 hours of transactions without data loss. Explain physical base backups (`pg_basebackup`), continuous WAL archiving (`archive_command` / WAL-G), and `recovery_target_time`.
expectedConcepts: Base backup + continuous WAL archive replay methodology
recovery.signal file and restore_command in PG 12+
recovery_target_action = pause for verification before promotion
hints: Why is a pg_dump logical backup alone insufficient for restoring to an exact microsecond?
How does recovery.signal tell PostgreSQL to enter recovery mode?
What parameter pauses replay so you can inspect data before promoting to write mode?
